messages.subject: NavbarPage and Markdown
parts:
Hi, 

I am using R.Studio a markdown document with embedded Shiny widgets. This works nicely:

---
title: "Untitled3"
runtime: shiny
output: html_document
---
``` {r, echo=FALSE}
dat <- data.frame(x=rnorm(100),y=rnorm(100),z=rnorm(100))
selectInput("dependent", "Dependent Variable:", c("x","y","z"))
runRegression <- reactive({
  lm(as.formula(paste(input$dependent," ~ y + z")),data=dat)
  })
renderTable({
  summary(runRegression())$coefficients
  
  })

```

This also works well:

``` {r, echo = F, eval=T}
navbarPage('This is a page',
  h4('Title')
  )
```

This gives an error: Error: object of type 'closure' is not subsettable:

``` {r, echo = F, eval=T}
navbarPage('This is a page',
          selectInput("dependent", "Dependent Variable:", c("x","y","z")),
           runRegression <- reactive({
             lm(as.formula(paste(input$dependent," ~ y + z")),data=dat)
             }),
           renderTable({
             summary(runRegression())$coefficients            
             })
           )
```

Same problem with tabsetPanel, with or without tabPanels
Any help would be greatly appreciated!

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: NavbarPage and Markdown
parts:
You were defining a reactive object runRegression() inside
navbarPage(), and you should not do that. For UI functions, please
only pass UI components to them. You can take out runRegression and
define it separately.

Regards,
Yihui
